model: REIT distributable income (AFFO) capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.48% vs revenue 7.95% (>30% divergence) and EPS is fair-value noise. Total-entity growth (revenue, equity, distributable income +4.7%/yr) has been bought with unit issuance and debt: per-unit DPU grew 0.4%/yr over 5 years and fell 0.6%/yr over 8. The per-unit series is the one that matters to a unitholder and is the one selected.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are stated on the per-unit distributable basis (DPU), the REIT analogue of owner FCF; management-fee units (~1.1% of revenue) and the sustaining-capex reserve are roughly constant shares of revenue so they do not change the growth rate. Reported OCF-capex CAGRs (0.5% 3yr, 6.7% 5yr) are total-entity and inflated by acquisitions. EPS CAGRs are meaningless (IAS 40 revaluations; FY2023 EPS 3.7c on a write-down).

scenario_narratives.base: Per-unit distributable income holds at ~15.0c in FY2026 as 1H26 acquisitions (Osaka data centre, Singapore industrial) fill the enlarged unit base, then grows 1.5-2% a year: high-single-digit rent reversions on a Singapore industrial market with tight supply are partly absorbed by occupancy stuck near 89-90% and by the external manager's habit of growing AUM without growing DPU. Debt cost stays ~3.5%, gearing ~39-40%. A 5%-of-revenue reserve covers sustaining capex and the slow run-off of JTC leasehold tenure.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data centre and logistics mix (9 Tai Seng, UK Golden Triangle greenfields, Japan) and the S$730m development pipeline lift per-unit growth to 3-4% in the next three years; occupancy recovers to 92-93% as redevelopment vacancies re-let; falling SORA/SOFR lets ~25% floating debt and maturing fixed tranches refinance cheaper, widening the DI margin to 46%. Tech-tenant demand (47% of rent) stays firm on AI capex. Per-unit growth settles at 2%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Bond yields keep rising through 2027, refinancing pushes cost of debt toward 4%+ and the DI margin to 41%; a tech-capex slowdown hits the 47% technology tenant base, occupancy slips below 89% and reversions fade to low single digits. Gearing near 40% forces equity-funded growth that is per-unit flat, ageing business parks need heavier capex (6% of revenue) and shortening Singapore leasehold tenures mean zero per-unit growth in perpetuity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A REIT unit is a claim on a post-interest distribution stream, so the stream (distributable income less the two costs S-REIT DI ignores: manager fees settled in units and sustaining/leasehold capex) is capitalised at the unitholders' cost of equity with no net-debt deduction. Growth is modelled per unit because CLAR's total-entity growth has historically been fully paid for with new units. NAV (S$2.29) is the cross-check: the market prices CLAR at ~0.97x NAV.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 50bp on the 7.25% CoE moves value roughly 8-10%; S-REIT prices track the 10y SGS yield
Unit count derived from 1H26 DI/DPU, not the unit register (interim not extracted)
Sustaining-capex/leasehold reserve (5% of revenue) is a judgment; the filings do not split maintenance from value-add capex
Distributable income can include discretionary items (divestment-gain distributions, fee-in-units add-backs) that are not recurring
Gearing ~39.7% vs 50% MAS limit; further acquisitions likely need equity, diluting per-unit growth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.14-2.92
data_sources.financials: A17U.SI_Metrics.csv (FY2017-FY2025, SGD millions) and kpis table (DistributableIncome, DistributionPerSecurity, NAVPerShare, ManagementFeesPaidInUnits); FY2025 Annual Report (units in issue line 6983, management fee in units line 7100, distributable income S$678.3m / DPU 15.005c line 506)
data_sources.qualitative: A17U.SI_Analysis.json (2026-10-24), including 1H FY2026 results figures (DI S$359.4m, DPU 7.482c, occupancy ~89.1%, leverage ~39.7%) not yet extracted from the interim filing

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash-flow / distribution adjustments line 7100: 'Management fee paid/payable in Units' S$17.644m (FY2024 S$17.258m). Treated as the REIT's SBC equivalent: it is expensed in the P&L, added back to distributable income as non-cash, and settled by issuing units to the external manager. Acquisition/divestment fees in units are capitalised/netted against deals and excluded.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:04:18Z (SGX regular session; Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,805m units = 1H FY2026 distributable income S$359.4m / 1H DPU 7.482 Singapore cents (Analysis JSON recent_developments, 1H 2026 results Aug 2026); cross-checks to 4,809m from 1H FY2025 units x 8.6% DI growth at flat DPU. FY2025 AR units in issue were 4,611.952m (31 Dec 2025); the ~193m increase funded 1H 2026 acquisitions (Greater Osaka data centre etc.). The 1H FY2026 interim filing is NOT in Extracted/, so this count is derived, not read off the register; replace with the register figure when the interim is extracted. Held flat: management-fee units are expensed in the flow, so diluting the count too would double-charge them. Acquisition-funding placements are NOT modelled; growth paths are therefore per-unit (organic plus accretion net of dilution), consistent with DPU of 15.7c (FY2017) -> 15.0c (FY2025) while revenue nearly doubled.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: the flow is distributable income, already after interest, perpetual-securities distributions, tax and land rent, so it is discounted at the unitholders' cost of equity and net debt is held at zero (subtracting S$7.1bn of net debt would deduct the debt twice). SGD build: 10y SGS ~2.6% (Oct 2026, after the 2026 bond-yield rise noted in the Analysis JSON) + levered beta ~0.85 x ERP 5.5% = ~7.3%; 7.25% used in all scenarios so risk is charged once, via the scenarios. Cross-check: 6.7% trailing DPU yield plus ~0.5-1% per-unit growth implies the market's CoE is ~7.2-7.7%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Land leases (S$604.8m lease liabilities, mostly JTC land rent on Singapore leasehold industrial sites) are inside distributable income (land rent is deducted in DI). Lease liabilities are therefore NOT in the bridge (net debt held at zero anyway). One treatment: in the flow.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI S$1.8m (FY2025) immaterial; distributable income is the unitholders' attributable figure, so NCI is already excluded from the flow.
inputs.perpetual_securities_treatment: Distributable income is after distributions to perpetual securities holders (S$10.0m FY2025; S$300m 3.18% green perps issued 2025), so the perps are charged once, in the flow, and do not appear in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT distributable-income (AFFO) capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine. Routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'REIT / property trust (IAS 40 fair-value, external manager)': CLAR is an externally managed S-REIT (manager CapitaLand Ascendas REIT Management, a CapitaLand Investment subsidiary) carrying 222+ properties at fair value (S$18.2bn FY2025, ~S$20.1bn 1H26). No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry -> first valuation. ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = gross revenue; 'ebitda_margin' = distributable income / gross revenue (FY2025 678.3/1538.6 = 44.1%; 1H26 359.4/~802 = 44.8%); 'sbc' = management fees paid in units (1.15% of revenue); 'capex' = sustaining capex + leasehold-tenure decay reserve at 5% of revenue (~S$77m, ~11% of DI) which S-REIT DI does NOT deduct -- Singapore assets (68% of value) sit on finite JTC leaseholds and business-park stock needs periodic redevelopment, so capitalising unadjusted DI in perpetuity overstates value; D&A 0 and cash tax 0 because DI is already post-tax. House AFFO FY2025 = 678.3 - 17.6 - 76.9 = 583.8 = last_fcf; reported_fcf carries distributable income. Growth/value-add capex (redevelopments, greenfield, S$730m pipeline) is funded by debt and unit issuance and its yield is captured in the revenue path, not charged as maintenance. NAV CROSS-CHECK: NAV/unit S$2.29 at 31 Dec 2025 (S$2.27 FY2024; 2.38 peak FY2021); price 2.23 = 0.97x NAV. BALANCE-SHEET VINTAGE: total_debt and cash are the 31 Dec 2025 audited figures; 1H26 aggregate leverage ~39.7% per the Analysis JSON (interim not extracted). Stated for information only -- net_debt is deliberately 0 in this model.

base.growth_rates_rationale: Year 1 +6.5% = FY2026 revenue on the enlarged unit base (1H26 gross revenue +6.3-6.7% YoY from S$1.15bn of 1H acquisitions incl. Greater Osaka DC); the 4,805m unit count already carries the units that funded them. Years 2-3 add full-year acquisition contribution and S$730m of developments completing to 2028 (~6-8% yields). Thereafter 1.5-2% per unit: high-single-digit reversions on ~25%/yr of expiring leases, offset by occupancy at ~89-90% and the history of zero per-unit accretion from external growth.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: Distributable income held at 44.0% of revenue = FY2026 DPU ~15.0c on 4,805m units (1H26 DPU 7.482c flat YoY). Cost of debt 3.5% with ~75% fixed; refinancing near current rates leaves the margin flat.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: 5% of revenue sustaining capex + leasehold decay reserve, not deducted in S-REIT DI.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: Caps (bear 15x / base 17x / bull 20x house AFFO) are set just above each scenario's Gordon multiple at the 7.25% CoE (13.8x / 16.2x / 19.4x) so Gordon governs; today's price is ~18.4x FY2025 house AFFO (14.9x DPU). A first build with 12/15/17x caps bound in every scenario and gave weighted S$2.07 -- the caps, not the CoE, were then setting the answer.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): DPU has been flat-to-down for eight years, gearing has drifted to ~39.7%, Net debt/EBITDA is 8.3x and the unit price is a direct function of SGD bond yields that rose in 2026. Base 50%: contracted rents, A3 rating, sponsor deal flow. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs falling rates, occupancy recovery and accretive per-unit deployment to all happen together, which this manager has not delivered historically.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
